name: Asset Purge Manager
description: Admin UI that lists every writable file in the public files directory and lets a privileged user select and delete them; files still tracked in file_managed are blanked (deleted then replaced with an empty file) rather than removed, to avoid dangling references.
project_description: Asset Purge Manager adds an administrative page that recursively scans the site's public files directory (the default file scheme) and lists every writable file in a paginated, selectable table. A privileged user can tick one or more files and delete them from disk. There is no automatic "unused/orphaned" detection: the page shows all writable files and leaves the judgement of what to remove to the operator. When a deleted file is still referenced in Drupal's file_managed table, the module does not simply remove it — it deletes the file and then re-creates it as an empty (zero-byte) placeholder, so managed-file references are not left dangling. Directories protected by an .htaccess containing 'Require all denied' (e.g. the private-style subtrees) are still listed but shown without a browsable link, since that link would 403. The module provides three permissions (page access, module administration, and the delete capability), a small config form to set how many files are shown per page, and menu/task links under Content and Configuration › Media. It ships no services, plugins, entities, hooks, or Drush commands — just two form classes.
